title: Allied Nations' Tour
src: Media.net OA, college not given (PDF write-up), problem 2.
body:
There are A cities in a row, numbered 1 to A. On day 0 you are in city B. On each of the days 1, 2, …, C you move from your current city i to any city in [i − E, i + E] (staying put is allowed; you can't leave the range 1..A).

You are warned of M attacks: D[k] = [day, city] means you must not be in that city on that day.

A tour is the sequence of cities you are in on days 1..C. Count the possible tours modulo 109 + 7.

Function to complete

Complete countTours(A, B, C, D, E). It returns the number of tours modulo 10^9 + 7.

Input reading and printing are handled for you, like on LeetCode. The input format below is what the tests and Custom input use.
inp: Line 1: A B C. Line 2: M. Then M lines: day city. Last line: E.
out: One integer: the number of tours modulo 10<sup>9</sup> + 7.

wrong.why: off by one: applies day d's attacks to day d + 1
sums the 2E+1 neighbours directly, O(A·C·E) (too slow)

samples.ex: Day 1: city 2 or 3 (city 1 is attacked). Day 2: from 2 you can reach 1, 2, 3; from 3 you can reach 2, 3. That is 5 tours.
City 3 is also attacked on day 2: from 2 you can go to 1 or 2, from 3 only to 2. 3 tours.

    D = [list(map(int, _t[_p + _i * 2:_p + (_i + 1) * 2])) for _i in range((_m))]; _p += (_m) * 2
    E = int(_t[_p]); _p += 1
    _r = Solution().countTours(A, B, C, D, E)
    print(_r)
